title: Starter examples reference
subtitle: Small site sources and annotated demonstrations
excerpt: Compare the four minimal examples and find their source files and annotated demonstrations.
content: These examples are for people who already use Jekyll. Each folder contains a Gemfile, _config.yml, home page and sample content. They have no deployment workflow. The separate Chulapa 101 template is a ready-made personal blog with publishing configured; it is not a selector for these four examples.                  Example       Included content       Annotated demo       Source                       Personal blog       A recent-post card index and a first story       Blog demo       personal-blog                 Technical blog       A post with code, Mermaid, MathJax and a TOC       Technical demo       technical-blog                 Portfolio       A projects collection, card index and two project pages       Portfolio demo       portfolio                 Project       A landing page with source and getting-started buttons       Project demo       project           The demos display source specimens and sample content inside this documentation site; they do not reproduce each standalone site’s home page or skin. The portfolio demo’s illustrative cards link to source files; the copied site’s cards link to generated project pages. The project demo’s Get started button opens fictional project copy, not the website setup guide.   All four folders have identical dependency lists: Jekyll ~> 4.4, remote-theme, include-cache, GitHub metadata, pagination, sitemap, the GFM Markdown parser, WEBrick, Windows timezone data and ostruct. The Gemfile installs dependencies; the configuration enables the listed plugins. Remote themes do not install gems.   The examples use the development remote theme with explicit dependencies. Mermaid requires development changes after v2.1.0. A portfolio’s cards do not provide filtering, and the project example does not supply a documentation sidebar.   For setup, use Run and publish a starter example. For a first website without local installation, use the browser tutorial.

title: Run and publish a starter example
subtitle: Set up one of the minimal Jekyll sites
excerpt: Copy a minimal example, preview it locally and configure its publication.
content: Use this guide when you already work with Jekyll and want to run one of the starter examples. You need Ruby, Bundler and an internet connection for gem installation and the remote theme download. The supplied Gemfiles use Jekyll ~> 4.4; keep each Gemfile together with its configuration. For a first site without installing software, use the browser tutorial.   The project example’s “Getting started” section is placeholder copy for the project you are presenting, not an installation procedure for this theme. The demos show annotated sources inside the documentation site; your copy uses the example’s own skin and generates its own article/project links.   Prepare your copy      Copy the contents of your selected example folder into your own site repository. Keep _posts or _projects at the site root, alongside _config.yml.   Edit the existing title, description and repository values in _config.yml. Set url to your site’s origin, such as https://ana.github.io, and baseurl to /my-blog for that repository’s site or "" for a site at the domain root.   Replace sample content and placeholder links. Blog posts go in _posts/YYYY-MM-DD-title.md; portfolio projects go in _projects/.   Keep the supplied design, or follow Choose a skin. To keep a released version, append a tag such as @v2.1.0 to remote_theme; Mermaid is unavailable in that release.   Preview the site   From your copied site’s directory, run:   bundle install bundle exec jekyll serve --url http://localhost:4000 --baseurl ""   Open http://localhost:4000. Check the home page, an article or project, and image and navigation links. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished. Restart Jekyll after editing _config.yml.   For the technical blog, also open its sample article and check the code, rendered diagram, equation and TOC links. Mermaid requires a modern browser with JavaScript modules/ES2024 support and access to jsDelivr; it is not included in v2.1.0. See diagram requirements and page feature options. For the portfolio, open both project cards; for the project landing page, check both buttons after replacing placeholder links.   Publish the site   Follow remote-theme publishing to configure GitHub Actions for your copy. The example folders do not include a publishing workflow; copying them does not publish a site.   Wait for the publishing run to succeed, then open the address in Settings > Pages. Check the same content and links on the public site, including its repository path.

title: Add or change a menu link
subtitle: Make an existing page reachable from your navbar
excerpt: Edit a menu label or destination without replacing your site's other navigation settings.
content: Use this guide when your site is already published and you have a page to link to. If the page does not exist yet, create it first. A menu entry does not create a page.   Edit the link      Open the page on your website and note its path. For the starter’s About page, use /about/. For a site at https://ana.github.io/my-blog/about/, the menu value is still /about/: the theme adds the site’s baseurl.   In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Find the existing navbar section and its nav list.   Change the matching entry’s title or url. If it is a new destination, add one entry to that list. Keep other links and the existing brand, style and expand settings. Do not add a second navbar section.   For example, the nav list for Home and About is:   navbar:   nav:     - title: Home       url: /     - title: About       url: /about/   This example shows the link list, not a replacement for your complete navbar section. Match the indentation of your existing entries and change the example label and path for your page.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Open the menu on a narrow screen and follow the edited link. Check that it opens the intended page, including on a site with a repository path.   If it opens a missing page, check the page’s published address and its permalink. If the old link remains, follow the publishing checks. For dropdown links and navbar style options, consult the navbar reference.

title: Edit footer links
subtitle: Update the contact, social or feed links below your pages
excerpt: Change footer labels and destinations, then verify the links on your published site.
content: Use this guide for an existing site with a contact address, social profile or feed you want visitors to open from the footer.   Edit the links      In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Find the existing footer section and its links list.   Edit a matching entry, or add an entry for a new destination. Keep other links and any existing copyright value. Do not add a second footer section.   Set a descriptive label and the destination url. Keep the entry’s existing Font Awesome icon, or choose one using the icon reference. Use the complete icon class value, such as fas fa-envelope for email.   For example, this list adds an email contact and the built-in Atom feed:   footer:   links:     - label: Email me       icon: fas fa-envelope       url: hello@example.org     - label: Subscribe to the feed       icon: fas fa-rss       url: /atom.xml   Replace the email address with your own. Email destinations use the plain address, without mailto:. A social link uses its full profile URL, such as https://github.com/your-account. A site-relative feed path is /atom.xml even when the website lives under a repository path; the theme adds the site’s baseurl.   The example shows only the links. Merge your changes into the existing list and preserve the other settings. To use a different feed, keep its actual published path; see feed compatibility.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch and wait for Actions to finish. Open the published website and scroll to the footer. Check every edited link: email should open your mail application, a profile should open the intended account, and a feed should return the feed document. A working feed link does not subscribe the visitor automatically.   If changes do not appear, follow the publishing checks. For the full option list and copyright behavior, use the footer reference.

title: Enable Fuse.js search
subtitle: Add a search page to an existing site
excerpt: Configure Fuse.js, publish a matching search page and check that visitors can find your content.
content: Use this guide for an existing site where you want Fuse.js search. The Chulapa 101 template already has it configured; check its existing search page before adding another. No provider account, API key or extra Jekyll plugin is needed for Fuse.js.   Configure the search page           In _config.yml, edit the existing search section, or add it once if absent:       search:   provider: fusejs   landing_page: /search           Keep any other search settings. If your current search has an established address, use that path for landing_page and for the page below.            Find your existing search page and edit it. If there is none, create search.md at the site root, alongside _config.yml, with this complete content:       --- layout: search title: Search permalink: /search ---           Keep only one page at this output address. The page’s permalink must match search.landing_page. For a site under /my-blog, use /search in both settings; the theme adds the site’s baseurl.            Save your changes on the publishing branch. Wait for Actions to finish, then open the search address directly. For a site at https://ana.github.io/my-blog, open https://ana.github.io/my-blog/search (or your chosen landing path).       Selecting a provider does not create the search page. The classic navbar and the desktop form of dual show a Search link only when navbar.nav is configured. If that link is absent, use the direct address above or configure your menu. The search layout supplies its own interface; extra page-body text is not displayed.   Check a result   Search for a distinctive word from a published article’s title. Follow the result and check that it opens the correct article, including on a repository-based site. Clear the search field and check that the results clear.   If the search page is missing, check its published address and the two matching settings above. If a document is absent from results, check its date, publishing status and any include_on_search: false in its front matter or defaults. Content changes enter the search index during the next site build; republish after edits.   To switch providers, use Lunr.js, Simple-Jekyll-Search, Google Custom Search or Algolia. For exact field defaults, use the search reference. For a working interface, see the Fuse.js demo.

title: Enable giscus comments on a post
subtitle: Connect GitHub Discussions and verify one published article
excerpt: Add the giscus embed, select the provider and enable comments on an existing post.
content: Use this guide for an existing post using layout: default and a GitHub repository you can configure for giscus. You need a public repository with Discussions enabled and the giscus app installed, as described by giscus setup. People posting comments through giscus sign in with GitHub.   Connect giscus      Open giscus setup, select your repository and discussion category, and choose how pages map to discussions. Copy the generated embed script with your actual repository and category identifiers.   In your site repository, create or edit _includes/custom/giscus.html. Paste that generated script into the file and save it. The template includes this file with a comment only; it needs your embed before comments can appear.        In _config.yml, edit the existing comments section, or add it once:       comments:   provider: giscus           Preserve unrelated settings and do not add a second comments section.            Open the post and set this entry between its existing --- lines:       show_comments: true           Keep its title, layout, date and other settings. Do not replace the whole front matter block. A provider selection alone does not enable the page.       Save all changes to your publishing branch, wait for Actions to finish, then open the article on your public website.   If you already have giscus discussions, keep their repository, category and page mapping choices unless you intend to change thread matching. Switching providers does not migrate comments between services.   Verify the comments area   Scroll below the article and check that the giscus interface loads. Sign in and, if appropriate, leave a test comment; confirm it appears in the selected repository’s Discussions. On other posts, comments remain controlled by their own front matter or existing defaults.   If nothing appears, check the embed file, comments.provider, the post’s show_comments value and its layout. Check giscus’s setup checks for app access, Discussions/category settings and domain restrictions. Browser blockers or a Content Security Policy can also stop the external embed from loading.   To enable more pages, set show_comments: true on those pages or merge it into an existing appropriate front matter default. For another existing service, use Disqus, Cactus, Welcomments or self-hosted Cusdis. Exact identifiers and constraints remain in the comments reference.

title: Change your site's name and author
subtitle: Update the identity of an already published site
excerpt: Edit your site title, description and author without changing its public address or other configuration.
content: Use this guide when your site is already published and you want to replace its sample name, description or author. For a first publication, use the browser tutorial.   Update the existing site settings   In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Find the existing title, description and author.name entries and change their values. For example:   title: "Ana's blog" description: "Travel stories and photographs" author:   name: "Ana"   Replace the example with your own details. Edit the existing entries instead of pasting a second section or replacing the whole file. Preserve other author fields, such as url, avatar, location and links, and keep their indentation.   Leave url, baseurl, repository and post addresses unchanged for this task. They identify your site’s location, not its display name. The template supplies the publishing path automatically. For a different hosting setup, consult the site settings reference.   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch.   Match the home-page heading   In the Chulapa 101 template, open the existing index.html file and change its title between the opening --- lines:   title: "Ana's blog"   Keep its filename, layout, other settings and content, then save. If your site uses a different home-page source, edit that existing file rather than adding or renaming an index. The page title supplies the visible heading separately from the site title.   Publish and check   Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open the address in Settings > Pages. Check your browser tab’s title and the home-page heading.   Check the author on a page that displays the site’s author, or in the automatic footer attribution. A page with its own author keeps that author; a custom footer.copyright is not rewritten when you change author.name. For those fields, use the author reference and footer reference.   The site description is metadata, not a replacement for the visible text of your pages. A page’s own description or excerpt can take precedence; see the description rules when checking a shared-page preview.   If the old values remain, follow the publishing checks. For local preview, restart Jekyll after editing _config.yml.

title: Create and publish a post
subtitle: Add an article to an existing site
excerpt: Create a dated Markdown post, publish it and check that readers can find it.
content: Use this guide when your site is already published. For a first website, follow the browser tutorial instead.   Create the file   In your repository’s Code tab, choose Add file > Create new file. Name it _posts/YYYY-MM-DD-my-first-post.md, replacing YYYY-MM-DD with today’s date or an earlier date, such as 2026-10-13. A future date normally keeps the post unpublished. Use a new filename so you do not replace an existing article.   Paste this complete example:   --- layout: default header_type: post title: "My first post" show_date: true ---  Welcome to my blog!  ## A place I visited  This is where my story begins. I can write **bold text** or add [a link](https://example.org/).   Replace the title and article text. Keep both --- lines: they enclose the page settings, also called front matter. Use ## for article sections; the layout already displays the main title.   To edit a sample post instead, open its existing file and click the pencil. Preserve settings you are not changing. The Markdown cheatsheet covers lists, tables and code; Add an image covers photographs.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. In the Chulapa 101 blog or personal-blog starter, follow the new article from the home-page post list. Check its title, date, sections and links.   Other site designs need a post index or a link to the published article. Post addresses depend on your site’s permalink setting; the file path under _posts is not its public address. Use your existing post index or generated site to find that address, then add a menu link if needed.   If the article is missing, check its filename and date, then follow the publishing checks. For optional page settings, use the layout reference.

title: Create a page and link it from the menu
subtitle: Publish a standalone page on an existing site
excerpt: Add a Contact page, give it a public address and make it reachable from your navbar.
content: Use this guide when your site is already published and you want a page such as Contact or About. Unlike a post, its filename does not need a date.   Create or edit the page   In your repository’s Code tab, choose Add file > Create new file. For the Chulapa 101 template, name the file _pages/contact.md. If it already exists, edit it instead of creating another page at the same address. You can also edit the starter’s _pages/about.md.   For a new Contact page, paste:   --- layout: default header_type: base title: "Contact" permalink: /contact/ ---  You can email me at [hello@example.org](mailto:hello@example.org).   Replace the sample email address and text. Keep both --- lines around the page settings, also called front matter. permalink sets the page’s public path. Keep /contact/ for this example and choose an unused path for other pages. When editing an existing page, preserve its address unless you intend to change links that already point to it.   For a site without the starter’s _pages setup, create contact.md beside _config.yml instead. You do not need a new collection or layout.   Add the menu link   Save the page with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Follow Add or change a menu link to add a Contact entry with url: /contact/ to your existing navbar list. Keep other links and settings. For a site under /my-blog, use /contact/, not /my-blog/contact/: the theme adds the repository path.   Publish and check   Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed. Open your website from Settings > Pages, then follow Contact from the menu, including on a narrow screen. Check the heading, text and email destination. Creating the file alone does not add it to the menu.   If the page returns 404, check that the file was saved and the menu path matches its permalink. Check for another file producing the same path, then use the publishing checks. For optional page settings, consult the layout reference.

title: Add an image to a post or page
subtitle: Upload a photograph and display it in your content
excerpt: Upload an image, use a repository-safe path and check the published result.
content: Use this guide when you already have a post or page to edit in a published site. For several images, use the gallery guide or slideshow guide instead.   Upload the file   Resize a large photograph before uploading it so visitors do not have to download the full original. In your repository’s Code tab, open assets/img/, choose Add file > Upload files, select your image and save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. If that folder does not exist, use GitHub’s upload page to drag a local assets folder containing img/river.jpg into the repository root. Preserve any existing files.   Use a simple filename such as river.jpg, without spaces. Keep the exact spelling, including uppercase and lowercase letters.   Insert it into the content   Open the post or page file and click the pencil. In the article text, below the settings block between --- lines, insert:   ![A riverside path beneath green trees]({{ '/assets/img/river.jpg' | relative_url }})   Replace the path with your uploaded file’s path. Keep relative_url: it adds the site’s repository path when needed. Do not add that prefix yourself. Replace the text in square brackets with a useful description of your image; readers who cannot see the photograph use that description.   Save the post or page with Commit changes on the same publishing branch.   Publish and check   Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed. Open the published article from your website, rather than relying on GitHub’s file preview. Check that the image loads and fits the content on a narrow screen.   If it is missing, compare the uploaded filename, extension and capitalization with the link. Verify both the image upload and article edit were saved, then follow the publishing checks. For captions, see the caption example. For video, use Embed a video.

title: Enable GoatCounter analytics
subtitle: Count visits on an existing published site
excerpt: Configure a GoatCounter counting address, publish in production and check a visit.
content: Use this guide when your site is already published and you have created a site in GoatCounter.   This integration requires Chulapa on main after v2.1.0. It is not included in the v2.1.0 release or gem.   Set the counting address   In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Find the existing goatcounter setting and edit it, or add it once if absent:   goatcounter: "https://YOUR-CODE.goatcounter.com/count"   Replace YOUR-CODE with your GoatCounter site’s code. Use the complete HTTPS counting address, including /count, rather than the dashboard address or just the code. A self-hosted site can use an address such as https://stats.example.org/count. Do not add your blog’s repository path to it. No API key or extra Jekyll plugin is needed.   If you want GoatCounter alone, clear existing gtag_id and analytics_id values. Otherwise the Google snippets also load. Remove any manually inserted copy of the same GoatCounter script from your custom includes to avoid counting a visit twice. Preserve unrelated settings.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Visit a page and check your GoatCounter dashboard; the visit may take a little time to appear. The integration counts page views; it does not display a visitor counter or configure custom events.   Counting is enabled only in a production build. For your own publishing workflow, check that it builds with Jekyll’s production environment. If you already preview locally with Jekyll, the equivalent build command is:   JEKYLL_ENV=production bundle exec jekyll build   Normal local preview does not load this tracker, and GoatCounter ignores localhost by default. Verify the published site instead.   If no visit appears      Check the theme version, production build and exact HTTPS counting address.   Check that a browser blocker has not blocked the tracker. Blocking it does not prevent your page from displaying.   If you configured a Content Security Policy, allow the script from https://gc.zgo.at/count.js and requests to your counting address.   For the service’s own counting rules and setup, consult GoatCounter help.   To disable the integration, leave goatcounter empty and publish again. For supported values and version constraints, use the analytics reference.

title: Enable Google Analytics 4
subtitle: Connect a published site to an existing GA4 web stream
excerpt: Set a measurement ID, publish and check the integration without adding a duplicate script.
content: Use this guide when your site is published and you have a Google Analytics 4 property with a web data stream for it. In Google Analytics, open Admin > Data streams, select that web stream and copy its Measurement ID, starting with G-.   Set the measurement ID   In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit the existing gtag_id entry, or add it once if absent:   gtag_id: G-XXXXXXXXXX   Replace the example with your own measurement ID. Preserve unrelated settings. Leave analytics_id empty: it is for retired Universal Analytics, not GA4. Do not paste an additional Google tag into your custom includes; the theme adds it from this setting. Remove a manually inserted duplicate of the same tracker.   If you want only Google Analytics, leave goatcounter empty. The two integrations are independent; configuring both loads both services.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Visit a page and check the Realtime report in the matching Analytics property. Allow time for reporting and check that you copied the ID from the intended stream.   A browser blocker or a site’s custom consent controls can prevent the tracking request. Check those controls if no visit appears. Unlike GoatCounter’s built-in integration, this Google tag is not restricted to production builds; an enabled ID also loads it during local preview.   To disable this integration, leave gtag_id empty and publish again. Also clear analytics_id if it still contains an old value. For the exact settings, use the Google Analytics reference.

title: Install using a remote theme
subtitle: Add the theme to an existing Jekyll site
excerpt: Configure a pinned remote theme, install its dependencies and verify your published site.
content: Use this guide when you already have a working Jekyll site, a Gemfile and Bundler available. For your first website, use the browser tutorial. If you are replacing another theme, follow the migration checklist to review content and old customizations as well.   Update your theme and dependencies   Work in a branch or save a backup. In _config.yml, remove the old theme entry and replace any existing remote_theme entry with:   remote_theme: dieghernan/chulapa@v2.1.0   This pins the released version. Use dieghernan/chulapa without the tag only when you want development updates from main. Features marked v2.1.1-dev are not included in v2.1.0.   In your existing Gemfile, add missing dependencies from the following list. Edit entries already present instead of declaring the same gem twice. Keep your existing Jekyll version, source, groups and other dependencies.   gem "jekyll-remote-theme" gem "jekyll-include-cache" gem "jekyll-github-metadata" gem "jekyll-paginate" gem "jekyll-sitemap" gem "kramdown-parser-gfm"   A remote theme downloads theme files; it does not install their Ruby dependencies. The personal-blog Gemfile is a complete Jekyll 4 example for a new local setup. Merge its dependencies with your own file rather than replacing a working site’s configuration.   In _config.yml, enable the following plugins in the existing list. Add the list once if absent, and retain other plugins your site needs:   plugins:   - jekyll-remote-theme   - jekyll-include-cache   From the directory containing your Gemfile, run:   bundle install bundle exec jekyll serve   Open the local address printed by Jekyll. Check the home page and an existing post or page. Restart the preview after changing _config.yml.   Local layouts, includes and matching assets override the theme. Review old copies if the design or behavior has not changed; downloading a new theme version does not replace them. See local override guidance.   Publish and check   For a site that already publishes successfully, retain its workflow and check that its build installs the dependencies from your Gemfile.   For a new GitHub Actions publishing setup, choose Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions and add a workflow under .github/workflows/. Use the template workflow as a starting point; adapt its branch, source directory and build settings to your repository. You do not need to copy the theme’s files into your site.   Commit to your publishing branch. Wait for the publishing run in Actions to succeed, then open the website address in Settings > Pages. On your published home page and a representative article, check the design, images, menu links and repository paths, including on a narrow screen.   For other hosts, use your existing deployment process after verifying the local build. If Jekyll reports an unknown include_cached tag, check that jekyll-include-cache is installed and enabled, then restart the build. Use Global settings to look up configuration fields.

title: Install using the theme gem
subtitle: Add the released theme to an existing Jekyll site
excerpt: Install the theme gem, enable its include-cache plugin and verify your build.
content: Use this guide when you already have a Jekyll site and use Bundler to build it. For a first website without local installation, follow the browser tutorial. The gem installs a published release; it does not provide unreleased features marked v2.1.1-dev.   Configure the gem   Work in a branch or save a backup. Add this entry to your existing Gemfile, or edit it if already present:   gem "chulapa-jekyll"   Keep your Jekyll and other site dependencies. Remove the old theme gem if it was only used by the theme you are replacing. In _config.yml, remove any remote_theme entry and replace the old theme value with:   theme: chulapa-jekyll   Enable jekyll-include-cache in the existing plugins list. The theme gem installs it as a dependency, but Jekyll still needs it enabled:   plugins:   - jekyll-include-cache   Preserve your other plugins and keep only one list. If switching from the remote method, remove jekyll-remote-theme from that list; remove its Gemfile entry if nothing else in your site needs it.   From the directory containing your Gemfile, run:   bundle install bundle exec jekyll serve   Open the local address printed by Jekyll. Check the home page and an existing post or page. Restart the preview after changing _config.yml.   Local layouts, includes and matching assets override the installed theme. Review copied files when changing or updating themes; installing a gem does not replace those copies. See local override guidance.   Publish and check   Commit your configuration and dependency changes, including Gemfile.lock if your repository tracks it. Use a publishing workflow that installs your bundle and builds with Jekyll. If setting up GitHub Actions, follow the publishing setup, keeping the gem-based theme setting from this guide.   Wait for the publishing run to succeed and open the deployed site. Check the home page, an article, images and menu links on a narrow screen. For a different host, use your existing deployment process. Review the migration checklist when replacing another theme.   To update only the theme and its dependencies, run:   bundle update chulapa-jekyll   Existing version constraints in your Gemfile still apply. Review release notes and local overrides, then repeat the preview and publication checks. For an unknown include_cached tag, check that jekyll-include-cache is installed and enabled before rebuilding.

title: Choose a skin
subtitle: Apply a predefined design to your site
excerpt: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab,open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserveunrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.
content: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.   Set the skin name   Choose a design from the skin previews. Use its exact lowercase name, then change the existing entry, for example:   chulapa-skin:   skin: journal   Keep other entries under chulapa-skin, including any vars overrides. Other choices include gitdev, lux and flatly. An unknown name prevents the site from building; selecting a preview in your browser does not save it to your site.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Check your home page and an article, including the menu on a narrow screen. Existing color/font overrides can keep parts of the previous appearance; see how skins and overrides interact before removing them. For local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml: these settings are compiled into CSS during the build. If changes are missing, use the publishing checks.   For an individual adjustment, use Change a color instead.

title: Change a color
subtitle: Override one design value without replacing the skin
excerpt: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab,open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserveunrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.
content: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.   Edit the color   Find the existing vars mapping under chulapa-skin, or add it once if absent. This example keeps the journal skin and changes its main color:   chulapa-skin:   skin: journal   vars:     primary: "#285d70"   Keep your own skin name if different. Quote values beginning with # and retain other overrides. For a specific component, use its name from the variable dictionary, such as navbar-chulapa-bg-color. A main-color change does not necessarily replace every color explicitly assigned by the skin; the precedence explanation describes why.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Check the changed component, text/link contrast and hover/focus states on your home page and an article. Check them on a narrow screen too; a color can affect more than one component. For local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml: these settings are compiled into CSS during the build. If changes are missing, use the publishing checks.   The appearance reference covers supported value syntax and calculated values that cannot be changed through vars.

title: Change the fonts
subtitle: Load a font stylesheet and apply its families
excerpt: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab,open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserveunrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.
content: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.   Each skin already has a font choice; changing fonts is optional. For the bundled font rather than an external stylesheet, use the bundled-font guide.   Load and apply the fonts   Choose families at Google Fonts and use their stylesheet URL. Add the URL to the existing googlefonts list, then set the families under your existing chulapa-skin.vars. For example:   googlefonts:   - url: "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Raleway&family=Rubik&display=swap"  chulapa-skin:   skin: journal   vars:     font-family-base: "Rubik, sans-serif"     headings-font-family: "Raleway, sans-serif"   Keep your selected skin and other variables. The stylesheet loads the families; font-family-base applies Rubik to body text and headings-font-family applies Raleway to headings. Loading a font alone does not apply it.   For another provider, place its stylesheet link in _includes/custom/custom_head.html following that provider’s instructions, then set the family variables as above. See custom head instructions.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Check body text and headings on your home page and an article. Confirm that text remains readable on a narrow screen. If a font is missing, check the family spelling and stylesheet URL; a blocker or network failure can prevent an external font from loading, leaving the fallback family. For local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml: these settings are compiled into CSS during the build. If changes are missing, use the publishing checks.   For all relevant fields, see the font reference.

title: Change code highlighting
subtitle: Apply a highlighting stylesheet to code blocks
excerpt: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab,open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserveunrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.
content: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.   Select the style   Choose a style from the highlighting previews. Change highlight under your existing chulapa-skin section:   chulapa-skin:   highlight: zenburn   Keep your skin and other settings. default is the default highlighting style. The preview selector changes only the demo, not your site’s configuration.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Open a page containing a fenced code block with a language name, such as ruby. Check the code text, background and contrast, including on a narrow screen. A highlighting style controls code appearance; it does not change the font or colors of ordinary article text. For local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml: these settings are compiled into CSS during the build. If changes are missing, use the publishing checks.   For the setting, see the highlighting reference.

title: How skins and overrides interact
subtitle: Understand which appearance settings take effect
excerpt: A skin provides a coordinated starting design. Individual variables customizethat design; Autothemer supplies a generated palette for values that are stillundefined. These choices affect appearance rather than the content layout.
content: A skin provides a coordinated starting design. Individual variables customize that design; Autothemer supplies a generated palette for values that are still undefined. These choices affect appearance rather than the content layout.   Why a color change can leave other colors unchanged   The selected skin supplies variable assignments first. Values in chulapa-skin.vars override those assignments. Autothemer follows, using defaults that preserve values already assigned by either source. Bootstrap and the theme’s components then use those values to produce the stylesheet.   That is why changing primary does not promise a complete recoloring of an existing skin. If it explicitly assigns a warning color or navbar background, that component can retain its own color. Autothemer fills gaps; it does not replace an existing palette. A skin written with !default allows subsequent configuration overrides while cooperating with the default palette.   Without an explicit skin/variable value, the navbar background uses primary; the footer and hero inherit the navbar background, and the landing page inherits the hero background. Many text colors are derived from backgrounds. Explicit component values take precedence over these defaults.   Variables and custom CSS serve different needs   A supported variable controls a design value used by the theme. Some helper values are calculated, including landingpage-card-bg and cactus-btn-text; they are not independent configuration inputs. Custom CSS is useful for rules that have no exposed variable. It loads after the theme stylesheet, although CSS specificity and individual rules still determine which declaration wins.   A local copy of a matching theme layout, include or asset takes precedence over the installed theme file. That can preserve a customization through an upgrade, but also keep an old implementation. A theme update does not automatically merge those copies. The same maintenance trade-off applies to a custom skin.   Choosing the right scope of change   A predefined skin suits a whole-site design choice. A variable override suits one color, font or component. A generated palette suits undefined colors that should relate to primary. A custom Sass skin suits a reusable set of assignments or rules; it carries more maintenance responsibility than a few config overrides.   For procedures, use Choose a skin, Change a color, Change fonts, Enable Autothemer or Adapt a Sass skin. The appearance reference and variable dictionary describe the inputs.

title: Enable Autothemer
subtitle: Generate colors that your skin has not already assigned
excerpt: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab,open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserveunrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.
content: Use this guide for an already published site. In your repository’s Code tab, open _config.yml and click the pencil. Edit existing entries and preserve unrelated settings; do not add a second chulapa-skin section.   Enable palette generation   Set autothemer to the YAML boolean true and supply a quoted main color. For a palette without a predefined skin’s color assignments, use none:   chulapa-skin:   skin: none   autothemer: true   vars:     primary: "#285d70"   none changes the selected skin; use it only if that is your intention. To keep your current skin, preserve its name instead. Autothemer can work with a skin, but it only fills undefined values. Existing skin colors and vars overrides remain in effect. Keep other custom variables unless you mean to remove them.   To stop this extra palette-generation step, omit autothemer or set it to false without quotes. A skin: auto selection separately loads the generator; the reference distinguishes the two settings.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Check the main color, backgrounds, warnings, errors and text contrast across your pages. If a color does not change, check whether your skin or vars already sets it. Use the precedence explanation to decide whether to change that variable explicitly. For local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml: these settings are compiled into CSS during the build. If changes are missing, use the publishing checks.

title: Adapt a Sass skin
subtitle: Preview existing Sass assignments and apply them to your site
excerpt: Use this guide when you already work with Sass/SCSS and have an existing Jekyllsite. Work in a branch or save a backup. For a built-in design, useChoose a skin; for one value, use Change a color.
content: Use this guide when you already work with Sass/SCSS and have an existing Jekyll site. Work in a branch or save a backup. For a built-in design, use Choose a skin; for one value, use Change a color. Preview the assignments Use the optional Codeply sandbox to preview assignments before applying them to your site. It requires working with Sass/SCSS; you can also apply the example directly and use your existing local Jekyll preview. Go to the Codeply sandbox The sandbox example includes INDEX and CLASSICNAVBARDEMO sections in the HTML panel for comparing navbar styles. Step-by-step example Let’s say we want to implement the Sunset theme by TopHat on our site. Having a look to the theme.scss, it looks like this: /*! Tophat `Sunset` Bootstrap 4.3.1 theme */ @import url(https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Voltaire:200,300,400,700); $headings-font-family:Voltaire; // Do not disable Bootstrap grid classes in the sandbox. $primary: #2F414A; $secondary: #F47B53; $success: #420084; $danger: #f2460d; $info: #7ebcfa; $warning: #ff9933; $light: #eef0f2; $dark: #000633; // Do not add a second Bootstrap import in the sandbox. // Add custom Sass rules here. 1. On the tool Open the sandbox and paste the font import and variable assignments above its existing imports in the CSS panel. Run the sandbox to preview Markdown and Bootstrap components. Modify until you are happy with your configuration. 2. On your _config.yml Translate that code as follows: googlefonts: - url: "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Voltaire:200,300,400,700" chulapa-skin: vars : primary: "#2F414A" secondary: "#F47B53" success: "#420084" danger: "#f2460d" info: "#7ebcfa" warning: "#ff9933" light: "#eef0f2" dark: "#000633" headings-font-family: Voltaire Sunset is already included: set chulapa-skin.skin: sunset to use the complete skin. The example above reproduces its palette and heading font through vars; it does not copy all of the skin’s CSS rules. Remove $ and ; when translating assignments, quote hex colors and leave a space after :. Alternatively, save your SCSS variables in _sass/skins/THEMENAME.scss, then set skin: THEMENAME inside chulapa-skin in _config.yml. Use !default for customizable skin variables. Autothemer fills undefined colors; omit a color from your skin if you want autothemer to derive it. Do not add a Bootstrap import: the theme imports Bootstrap after loading the skin. See the Sunset skin source. To contribute a skin, open a pull request. Using autothemer on Codeply Autothemer is already installed in the ply. To activate it, uncomment the lines between /* Start autothemer */ and /* End autothemer */ on the CSS window. Keep the theme’s Bootstrap import and grid enabled. Do not add another @import "bootstrap"; to your skin. Setting $enable-grid-classes: false removes grid classes used by the theme and breaks its layouts. Publish and check Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for the latest run in Actions to succeed, then open your website from Settings > Pages. Check the translated colors and heading font on your home page and an article, including menu controls, grids and text contrast on a narrow screen. If you created a local skin, ensure its filename matches chulapa-skin.skin exactly. The palette-only example does not copy all original skin CSS rules....

title: Add a photo gallery
subtitle: Group uploaded photographs in a masonry gallery
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing post or page that uses a theme layout and canalready display an image. To upload a single photograph first, seeAdd an image.
content: Use this guide for an existing post or page that uses a theme layout and can already display an image. To upload a single photograph first, see Add an image.   Version requirement: this filename-order recipe requires main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), or a later release containing the sorting fix. The v2.1.0 gem and pinned remote theme do not correctly apply the selected index_sort field, so numbered filenames alone do not guarantee this order.   Group the photographs   Upload your photographs into assets/img/gallery/ in your repository. In _config.yml, append this entry to the existing defaults list; keep all other entries. If defaults already exists, append only the - scope entry below, not a second defaults: key. If the list does not exist, add the complete block:   defaults:   - scope:       path: "assets/img/gallery"     values:       image_col: gallery   Use filenames such as 01-coast.jpg and 02-harbour.jpg to choose an order.   Insert the gallery   In the Markdown body of your post or page, add:   {% include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" index_sort="basename" index_sort_asc=true %}   The group name must match image_col. These parameters belong in the include call, not in the settings block at the top of the page.   Gallery snippets generate generic image descriptions. For photographs that need individual descriptions, use image markup with descriptive alternative text and accompanying captions instead.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the site from Settings > Pages. Check the published page, not only GitHub’s file preview. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks.   Check that every photograph appears in filename order and that the gallery fits a narrow screen. If it is empty, check the uploaded folder, defaults path and group name. If your files use a different folder, adapt that path in defaults.   To open images in a viewer, follow Enable PhotoSwipe. For external image lists, sorting, limits and a runnable specimen, see the gallery reference.

title: Add a manual slideshow
subtitle: Display an image group with previous and next controls
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing post or page. First upload and group photographsfollowing Add a photo gallery. Keep thesame image_col: gallery group; a custom layout must load Bootstrap’s scriptsfor slideshow controls to work.
content: Use this guide for an existing post or page. First upload and group photographs following Add a photo gallery. Keep the same image_col: gallery group; a custom layout must load Bootstrap’s scripts for slideshow controls to work.   Version requirement: this recipe’s filename ordering and keyboard-operable buttons and indicators require main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), or a later release containing those fixes. In v2.1.0, the sort field is not applied correctly, indicators cannot receive keyboard focus and previous/next links do not activate with Space.   Insert a carousel   Add this to the Markdown body of your page, replacing a masonry include if you want to display the same photographs only once:   {% include_cached snippets/carousel.html internal="gallery" index_sort="basename" index_sort_asc=true interval=0 controls=true indicators=true %}   This starts with manual navigation. Pass 0 without quotes to stop automatic cycling; pass true without quotes for the controls and slide indicators.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the site from Settings > Pages. Check the published page, not only GitHub’s file preview. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks.   Check the previous/next buttons and indicators on a narrow screen. Use Tab to reach each control and Enter or Space to activate it. An empty slideshow usually means the folder or image_col group does not match the include.   For optional automatic cycling, timing and control colors, see the carousel reference. For a zoomable viewer, follow Enable PhotoSwipe.

title: Enable PhotoSwipe on a gallery
subtitle: Open gallery images in a zoomable viewer
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing gallery orcarousel.
content: Use this guide for an existing gallery or carousel.   Version requirement: PhotoSwipe is available on main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), not in the v2.1.0 gem or a remote theme pinned to that release.   Enable the viewer   In the Markdown body of your page, find its existing gallery include and add photoswipe=true, preserving the other parameters. For example:   {% include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true %}   For a carousel, add the same parameter to its existing include:   {% include_cached snippets/carousel.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true controls=true interval=0 %}   Use the boolean true without quotes. This is an include parameter, not a page or site YAML setting. If your site has a Content Security Policy, allow scripts and styles from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the site from Settings > Pages. Check the published page, not only GitHub’s file preview. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks.   Open an image, try the viewer’s controls and press Escape to close it. Check that keyboard focus returns to the image. Also try swiping on a touch device when available. If the viewer cannot load, the image link opens the original file.   Try the live PhotoSwipe demo. For supported image sources, loading behavior and accessibility constraints, see the PhotoSwipe reference.

title: Embed a video
subtitle: Add a named YouTube player to a post or page
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page that uses a theme layout.Have the YouTube video’s address and title ready.
content: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page that uses a theme layout. Have the YouTube video’s address and title ready.   Add the player   In the body of your post or page, insert the following line. Replace the id with the video identifier and name with its title. The identifier is the same in these common address formats:                  YouTube address       Value for id                       https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1hXYuWTWVww       1hXYuWTWVww                 https://youtu.be/1hXYuWTWVww?si=example       1hXYuWTWVww                 https://www.youtube.com/shorts/1hXYuWTWVww       1hXYuWTWVww           For a watch address use the value after v=; for Share or Shorts addresses use the final path segment. Leave out query parameters such as si or t, and any # fragment. For example:   {% include snippets/video.html provider="youtube" id="1hXYuWTWVww" name="Menorca - Isla Bonita" %}   Do not paste the entire watch URL into id. The player initially shows a preview; a visitor activates it to load YouTube. If your Content Security Policy restricts frames, allow https://www.youtube-nocookie.com.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the site from Settings > Pages. Check the published page, not only GitHub’s file preview. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks.   Check the preview and activate it to play the video. Reach the preview with Tab and activate it with Enter. Supply a nearby text summary or transcript and use captioned media where needed; the theme does not create captions or transcripts.   If the preview image is unavailable, add video_res="hqdefault" to the include and check again. If playback is blocked, check the video’s embedding permissions and browser or network restrictions.   For other supported providers, a hosted MP4, immediate iframe loading or video metadata, use the video reference and metadata fields. thumbnail_url describes the video to search engines; it does not replace the visible preview.

title: Add a Mermaid diagram
subtitle: Render an accessible flowchart in a post or page
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with the default layoutor another layout based on minimal. The search layout does not display pagecontent.
content: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with the default layout or another layout based on minimal. The search layout does not display page content.   Version requirement: Mermaid is available on main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), not in the v2.1.0 gem or a remote theme pinned to that release.   Enable and insert the diagram   Add mermaid: true to the existing settings block between --- lines at the top of your page. Preserve the other fields. Then insert a mermaid fenced block in the body. A complete page example:   --- layout: default title: My publishing workflow mermaid: true ---  ```mermaid flowchart LR   accTitle: Publishing workflow   accDescr: Write content, build the site and publish it.   A[Write] --> B[Build] --> C[Publish] ```  Saving an article starts the build; a successful build publishes the website.   Adapt the labels and accessible description to your diagram. Keep a prose explanation for complex diagrams.   Publish and check   Save with Commit changes on your publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the site from Settings > Pages. Check the published page, not only GitHub’s file preview. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks.   Use a modern browser with JavaScript modules and ES2024 support (Safari 17.4 or later). Check that the flowchart replaces the code and fits the page; wide charts can scroll horizontally. If code remains visible, check mermaid: true, the fence spelling and diagram syntax, then check whether the CDN or JavaScript is blocked. Mermaid loads from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net.   Try the live Mermaid demo. For the library version, security restrictions and fallback behavior, see the Mermaid reference.

title: Enable Lunr.js search
subtitle: Configure local search on an existing site
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing site. No search-service account, API key oradditional Jekyll plugin is needed. The personal-blog template already usesFuse.js; follow these steps only if you want to replace that provider.
content: Use this guide for an existing site. No search-service account, API key or additional Jekyll plugin is needed. The personal-blog template already uses Fuse.js; follow these steps only if you want to replace that provider.   Configure the provider and page   In _config.yml, edit the existing search section, or add it once if absent:   search:   provider: lunr   landing_page: /search   Preserve other search settings. If your search page already has another address, keep that path in landing_page and in the page below.   Edit the existing search page. If there is none, create search.md next to _config.yml with this content:   --- layout: search title: Search permalink: /search ---   Keep only one page at that address. permalink and search.landing_page must match; do not prepend the site’s baseurl to either value. The search layout supplies the interface and does not display page-body text.   Publish and verify   Save with Commit changes on the publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open your site’s search address. For a site at https://ana.github.io/my-blog, the default address is https://ana.github.io/my-blog/search.   Search for a distinctive word from a published article’s title, open a result and verify its address. Clear the field and check that the results clear. If a result is missing, check the document’s publication status and date, and any include_on_search: false in its settings or configuration defaults. The index updates during a site build; publish again after content changes.   The classic navbar and desktop dual navbar show the Search link only when navbar.nav is configured. If it is absent, use the direct address above or edit your menu. If the page itself is missing, check the build and matching paths; see publishing checks.   For word limits, attribution and legacy settings, use the search reference.
