title: Enable Google Custom Search
subtitle: Connect an existing Google search engine to your site
excerpt: Use this guide if you already have a Google Custom Search engine configured foryour site’s public address. Obtain its engine ID from yoursearch engine settings.For search without a service account or external indexing, useFuse.js instead.
content: Use this guide if you already have a Google Custom Search engine configured for your site’s public address. Obtain its engine ID from your search engine settings. For search without a service account or external indexing, use Fuse.js instead.   Connect the engine   In _config.yml, edit the existing search section and google_cse_id, or add them once if absent. Replace the example engine ID with yours:   search:   provider: google   landing_page: /search google_cse_id: "YOUR_SEARCH_ENGINE_ID"   Keep other settings and the established search address if there is one. Reuse its existing page; if absent, create search.md next to _config.yml:   --- layout: search title: Search permalink: /search ---   The page’s permalink must match search.landing_page. Do not add the site’s baseurl to those values, and do not create a second page at the same address. No extra Google embed script belongs in the page; the theme provides it.   Publish and verify   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published search address. Search for a distinctive title from a public page already indexed by Google; follow a result and check its destination.   If the interface fails to load, check the engine ID and browser/network blockers. If results are missing or cover the wrong sites, check the engine’s configured site scope and Google’s indexing. A successful Jekyll build does not upload an index to Google; include_on_search controls the local providers, not Google’s crawler. If the Search menu link is missing, visit the address directly or configure your menu.   For field names, defaults and other providers, use the search reference.

title: Connect Algolia search and upload its index
subtitle: Configure browser search and a separate indexing step
excerpt: Use this guide if you already have an Algolia application/index and maintainyour site’s Jekyll build workflow. Have the application ID, index name, publicsearch-only key and separate indexing key ready. For a simpler search withoutan account or index-upload workflow, use Fuse.js.
content: Use this guide if you already have an Algolia application/index and maintain your site’s Jekyll build workflow. Have the application ID, index name, public search-only key and separate indexing key ready. For a simpler search without an account or index-upload workflow, use Fuse.js. Compatibility: the theme’s jekyll-algolia indexing plugin is deprecated and no longer maintained by Algolia. Check its compatibility with your build before adopting it; keep an existing working setup while testing changes. Configure browser search In _config.yml, edit the existing mappings, or add each once if absent. Replace the three example values with your account’s values: search: provider: algolia landing_page: /search algolia: application_id: "YOUR_APPLICATION_ID" index_name: "YOUR_INDEX_NAME" search_only_api_key: "YOUR_PUBLIC_SEARCH_ONLY_KEY" Preserve other settings, particularly existing Algolia exclusions and ranking. Keep your current search address if different. Reuse the page at that address; if absent, create search.md next to _config.yml: --- layout: search title: Search permalink: /search --- Match permalink to search.landing_page without adding baseurl. Keep only one output page at that address. Selecting Algolia does not create the page or upload an index. Upload the index In the site’s Gemfile, add this gem inside the existing :jekyll_plugins group if it is missing; preserve the other gems. If the group does not exist, add the complete block: group :jekyll_plugins do gem "jekyll-algolia", "~> 1.0" end Run bundle install in the site directory and commit the updated Gemfile and Gemfile.lock. In your existing GitHub Actions build workflow, after checkout, Ruby setup and dependency installation, add this step. It assumes _config.yml is at the repository root: - name: Upload Algolia index run: bundle exec jekyll algolia env: ALGOLIA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ALGOLIA_API_KEY }} In the repository’s Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions, add the indexing key as the repository secret ALGOLIA_API_KEY. If your site source is in a subfolder, set the step’s working-directory to the folder containing its Gemfile and _config.yml, following your existing workflow. Keep the indexing key private. Only the public search-only key belongs in _config.yml. Never put the indexing key in a file or browser script. The index-upload step sends site content to Algolia: review exclusions first. Use algolia.files_to_exclude for content that must stay out of this index; include_on_search: false is not an Algolia exclusion. The sample’s customRanking merely uses that field for ranking. See the indexing option reference and plugin options. An alternative workflow is the Algolia Jekyll action; adapt its source directory and credentials to your site rather than running both upload methods. Publish and verify Commit to the publishing branch. Confirm that the publishing workflow and index upload both succeed. In Algolia, verify that the expected index contains records and that excluded content is absent. Open the published search page, search for a distinctive article title and follow a result. Verify its public address, including any repository path. For no results, check that the uploaded index name/application match the browser settings and that the key is search-only with access to that index. For stale results, check the upload run after the latest content change. Browser/network blockers can prevent...

title: Connect Disqus comments
subtitle: Enable an existing Disqus site on one post
excerpt: Use this guide if you already have a site registered with Disqus.Have its shortname ready: the identifier inhttps://YOUR_SHORTNAME.disqus.com/admin/, not the site’s display name.
content: Use this guide if you already have a site registered with Disqus. Have its shortname ready: the identifier in https://YOUR_SHORTNAME.disqus.com/admin/, not the site’s display name.   Select Disqus   In _config.yml, edit the existing comments section, or add it once if absent. Replace the example shortname and preserve unrelated settings:   comments:   provider: disqus   disqus_shortname: "YOUR_SHORTNAME"   Do not paste a second embed script into your post; the theme supplies it.   Enable one post   Open an existing post using layout: default. Add or update this value between its existing --- lines, preserving the title, date, layout and other settings:   show_comments: true   Selecting a provider alone does not enable comments on the page. Save all changes on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the article on your public website.   Verify the discussion   Scroll below the published article and check that the Disqus interface loads. If appropriate, post a test comment and confirm it is associated with that article in your Disqus administration panel.   If you had comments before switching themes, check an existing discussion as well. The theme supplies the page URL and identifier automatically; identical URLs alone do not guarantee identical identifiers across themes. Preserve your shortname and established URLs, and check Disqus’s migration tools if threads are mismatched. Switching providers does not transfer comments.   If no interface appears, check the shortname, show_comments, layout and publishing run. Browser blockers or a Content Security Policy may block the external embed; inspect failed requests before changing your policy.   For more posts, set show_comments: true individually or merge it into an appropriate existing front matter default. Other providers and exact fields are in the comments reference.

title: Connect Cactus comments
subtitle: Enable an already registered Cactus site on one post
excerpt: Use this guide after registering your site with Cactus.Have its registered site name ready. This adapter uses the Cactus-hosted Matrixservice; there is no theme setting for selecting an arbitrary Matrix homeserver.
content: Use this guide after registering your site with Cactus. Have its registered site name ready. This adapter uses the Cactus-hosted Matrix service; there is no theme setting for selecting an arbitrary Matrix homeserver.   Adapter limitation: the current theme passes page URLs containing / to Cactus, whose client requirements exclude / and _ from conversation IDs. Configure the local correction below before relying on this integration, including on v2.1.0.   Select Cactus   In _config.yml, edit the existing comments section, or add it once if absent. Replace the example site name and preserve unrelated settings:   comments:   provider: cactus   cactus_shortname: "YOUR_REGISTERED_SITE_NAME"   Keep the theme’s Cactus integration; do not add another embed to the post.   Correct the conversation identifier   Copy _includes/components/cactus.html from your installed theme version into the same path in your repository. The development source shows the file’s structure. Preserve the rest of the file and replace only its commentSectionId line with:       commentSectionId: "{{ include.pageurl | url_encode | replace: '_', '%5F' }}"   This encodes / and _ without collapsing distinct paths such as /a/b/ and /a-b/ into one conversation ID. The same page URL always produces the same ID. Keep the local file under review when upgrading the theme.   Existing conversations: changing an ID can disconnect an old thread. Record the IDs used by your existing integration and check their matching before publishing this override. If they differ, arrange migration with the provider or retain the existing valid mapping in your local adapter. Changing the theme’s identifier does not move Matrix conversations automatically.   Enable one post   Open an existing post using layout: default. Add or update this value between its existing --- lines, preserving the title, date, layout and other settings:   show_comments: true   Selecting a provider alone does not enable comments on the page. Save all changes on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the article on your public website.   Verify the discussion   Scroll below the article and check that the comment interface loads. If appropriate, submit a test comment through the provider’s interface and verify that it belongs to this article. Check an existing thread when upgrading; keep the registered site name, established page addresses and verified conversation ID mapping. Changing providers does not migrate comments.   If the area is missing, check the registered site name, show_comments, layout and publishing run. Check external script/network failures and any Content Security Policy or browser blocker before changing the setup.   In main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), Cactus scripts and styles load only on pages with show_comments: true. That loading improvement is not in v2.1.0; the identifier correction above is still required for this guide on that release.   For more posts, set show_comments: true individually or merge it into an appropriate existing front matter default. Other providers and exact fields are in the comments reference.

title: Connect Welcomments
subtitle: Keep theme templates while connecting an existing website
excerpt: Use this guide if you already have a website configured withWelcomments, its website ID and a working integrationthat delivers comment files to this repository. Configure that service-sideintegration using the provider’s instructions before testing new submissions.
content: Use this guide if you already have a website configured with Welcomments, its website ID and a working integration that delivers comment files to this repository. Configure that service-side integration using the provider’s instructions before testing new submissions.   Review the integration files   Review any pull request generated by Welcomments before merging it. Retain the customized _includes/welcomments/ templates supplied by Chulapa, rather than replacing them with generic provider templates. Review any local copies left by another theme: local files override the installed theme’s files.   Keep the provider’s comment data and repository integration. The theme reads comment data from _data/welcomments/; the website ID alone does not deliver that data or configure the external service.   Select Welcomments   In _config.yml, edit the existing comments section, or add it once if absent. Replace the example website ID and preserve unrelated settings:   comments:   provider: welcomments   website_id: "YOUR_WELCOMMENTS_WEBSITE_ID"   Check the form URL on a project site   The current theme form builds its permalink without baseurl. If your site is under a path such as https://ana.github.io/my-blog, the submitted URL can point outside /my-blog. Check this before using the integration.   For a site with baseurl, copy the theme’s customized form to _includes/welcomments/comment_form.html in your repository. Use the file from your installed theme version; the linked main file is the development version. Preserve the rest of that file; replace only the hidden permalink input with:   <input type="hidden" name="permalink" id="permalink" value="{{ page.url | absolute_url }}">   When you publish the post below, inspect its hidden permalink value in your browser’s developer tools. It must match the full article address, including the project path. Keep this local override under review when upgrading the theme.   Enable one post   Open an existing post using layout: default. Add or update this value between its existing --- lines, preserving the title, date, layout and other settings:   show_comments: true   Selecting a provider alone does not enable comments on the page. Save all changes on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the article on your public website.   Verify the form and saved comment   Check the form below the article. If appropriate, submit a test comment, verify that the service delivers its data to your repository, then check that a successful site rebuild displays it. A temporary browser placeholder is not proof that the comment has reached the published static site.   If the form is missing, check the website ID, show_comments, layout and local template overrides. If a submitted comment never appears after a rebuild, check the provider’s repository integration and delivered data, and confirm that the post’s slug still matches its existing comment data. Renaming a post can change that match; switching providers does not transfer old comments automatically.   For more posts, set show_comments: true individually or merge it into an appropriate existing front matter default. Other providers and exact fields are in the comments reference.

title: Connect an existing self-hosted Cusdis service
subtitle: Configure the host and application ID for one post
excerpt: Use this guide only if you already operate a working self-hosted Cusdis serviceand have its host URL and application ID.
content: Use this guide only if you already operate a working self-hosted Cusdis service and have its host URL and application ID.   Compatibility: Cusdis is deprecated and archived; its original hosted service is unavailable. This guide connects an existing deployment, not a new hosted account. For another supported provider, see giscus or the comments reference.   Connect the host   In _config.yml, edit the existing comments section, or add it once if absent. Replace the example URL and ID with values from your service’s embed code:   comments:   provider: cusdis   cusdis_host: "https://comments.example.com"   cusdis_app_id: "YOUR_APPLICATION_ID"   Use the host’s HTTPS base URL, not a script URL. Preserve unrelated settings. Keep your existing application ID and page addresses when reconnecting old threads. Do not add a second Cusdis embed script; the theme supplies its adapter.   Enable one post   Open an existing post using layout: default. Add or update this value between its existing --- lines, preserving the title, date, layout and other settings:   show_comments: true   Selecting a provider alone does not enable comments on the page. Save all changes on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the article on your public website.   Verify the connection   Check that the comment interface loads from your host below the article. If appropriate, submit a test comment and verify it in your service. Check existing threads too; the theme supplies page identifiers automatically, so a change of theme or provider may require service-side thread matching. Comments do not migrate automatically between providers.   If it does not load, verify the host and app ID, show_comments, layout and site build. Check failed requests to your host, HTTPS/mixed-content errors, browser blockers and any Content Security Policy. Omitting cusdis_host uses the old https://cusdis.com default; it does not select your self-hosted service.   For more posts, set show_comments: true individually or merge it into an appropriate existing front matter default. Other providers and exact fields are in the comments reference.

title: Find changes missing from your website
subtitle: Check the saved edit, publishing run and public address
excerpt: Use this guide when you have edited your site’s files but the public websitestill shows old content or a new article is missing. Keep the existing setupwhile checking the steps below.
content: Use this guide when you have edited your site’s files but the public website still shows old content or a new article is missing. Keep the existing setup while checking the steps below.   Check the saved edit and branch   In the repository’s Code tab, open the edited file. Confirm that your change is saved in a commit, not only in the editor. Check the branch selector: the starter publishes from main or master. For another setup, check the publishing workflow or Settings > Pages for its source.   If your edit is on a separate branch or an unmerged pull request, use your normal review/merge process to place it on the publishing branch. A preview site and the public website can show different commits.   Check the publishing run   Open Actions and find the publishing run for that commit and branch. Wait for it to finish. If it fails, open the failed step and read the first relevant error; do not change unrelated settings to try to fix it.   For a _config.yml syntax error, follow Fix a YAML configuration error. For missing plugins or theme dependencies, use your installation method or the migration checks.   Check the right website   Open the website address in Settings > Pages, then refresh the affected page. Check that you are visiting the public site rather than GitHub’s file preview or another deployment. For a project site, retain its repository path. If the build succeeded but publication failed, inspect the deployment step too.   For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. A successful local build alone does not publish those files to GitHub Pages.   Check a missing post   Verify the file is in _posts/ and named YYYY-MM-DD-title.md, with a real, non-future date. Check any explicit date or published: false in its settings as well. Normal builds omit future-dated and unpublished posts.   Use Create a post to compare the file structure. Check its actual public address, including any permalink: the Markdown source path is not the post URL. If the article opens directly but is absent from an index, check that index’s filters and limits in the layout reference. For a missing photograph, use the image checks.   After correcting the identified problem, commit to the publishing branch, wait for a successful deployment and verify the changed text or article again.

title: Fix a YAML configuration error
subtitle: Correct the edit that stopped the site build
excerpt: Use this guide when your publishing run or local preview reports a YAML error,especially after editing _config.yml or a post’s settings block.
content: Use this guide when your publishing run or local preview reports a YAML error, especially after editing _config.yml or a post’s settings block.   Locate the failed edit   Open the failed run in Actions, then its failed build step. Note the filename and line mentioned in the error. Compare that area and the preceding lines with your last commit; a missing quote can make the parser report a later line.   For a local setup, run bundle exec jekyll build in your site directory to see the error. You do not need a local installation just to read the Actions log.   Correct the formatting   Edit the existing file rather than replacing it with a full sample configuration. Use spaces for indentation, keeping sibling settings aligned. Complete any unclosed quotes and remove duplicate top-level sections by merging their entries.   Quote text containing a colon followed by a space, for example:   title: "Notes: fieldwork"   Quote hexadecimal colors so # is not interpreted as a comment. For example, within your existing chulapa-skin.vars mapping:   primary: "#285d70"   Keep the surrounding indentation when applying that line; do not create a second chulapa-skin mapping. Use actual booleans such as false, not the string "false", for boolean settings.   A YAML checker can help locate formatting mistakes. A syntax pass alone does not prove the configuration is correct: check duplicate keys and compare skin names, provider identifiers and field locations with Global settings and Theming.   Rebuild and verify   Commit the correction to the publishing branch and check the next Actions run. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. Once the build and deployment succeed, check the changed setting on the public website. If parsing succeeds but the setting has no effect, inspect its documented location and defaults rather than repeatedly changing the YAML formatting.

title: Add custom HTML to the page head
subtitle: Use a supported hook without copying a layout
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing site using the theme’s layouts. Have the HTMLsnippet you want in <head> ready. For Google Analytics or GoatCounter, usethe analytics guides and GA4 guideinstead of installing the same script twice. Check their version requirements.
content: Use this guide for an existing site using the theme’s layouts. Have the HTML snippet you want in <head> ready. For Google Analytics or GoatCounter, use the analytics guides and GA4 guide instead of installing the same script twice. Check their version requirements.   Edit the head hook   In your repository, create or edit _includes/custom/custom_head.html. Keep existing snippets in the file. Append the HTML required by your provider; no YAML front matter or layout copy is needed in this include.   For a small example, this adds application-name metadata:   <meta name="application-name" content="Field Notes">   Replace Field Notes with your site’s name, or use the actual snippet required by your provider. The hook inserts HTML after the theme’s stylesheets, near the end of <head>. Do not paste an entire HTML document into it.   If the provider specifically requires insertion before CSS or at the end of <body>, choose the corresponding file in the hook reference and follow that provider’s dependency/loading instructions instead.   Publish and verify   Commit on the publishing branch and wait for Actions to finish successfully. Open an article on the website and inspect its HTML source: the sample meta tag, or your snippet, must appear inside <head>. Also check a search page if your site has one; the hook works with the built-in minimal and search layouts.   If it is missing, check the filename, leading underscore in _includes, branch and deployment. Review any local layout or head include that overrides the theme. If the HTML appears but a third-party script fails, inspect its network errors, provider configuration and any browser or Content Security Policy restrictions. For an old public page, follow the publishing checks.   CSS rules belong in assets/css/custom.scss, with its empty YAML front matter retained, rather than as raw CSS text in this HTML include. See the supported files.

title: Custom hooks reference
subtitle: File paths, insertion points and override constraints
excerpt: Lookup for site-wide custom files. For an editing procedure, useAdd custom HTML to the page head.
content: Lookup for site-wide custom files. For an editing procedure, use Add custom HTML to the page head.                  Site-relative path       Content       Insertion point or output                       _includes/custom/custom_head_before_css.html       HTML       Inside <head>, before the theme stylesheet.                 _includes/custom/custom_head.html       HTML       Near the end of <head>, after the theme stylesheet.                 _includes/custom/custom_bottomscripts.html       HTML       At the end of <body>, after theme JavaScript dependencies.                 assets/css/custom.scss       CSS/SCSS with empty YAML front matter       Compiles to assets/css/custom.css, loaded by the theme head.           Scope and precedence   Matching local files override theme files with both remote_theme and the gem. The three HTML hooks require no YAML front matter. Existing snippets in an individual hook remain the site’s responsibility; replacing that file replaces its contents. No new configuration flag enables these hooks.   The built-in minimal layout and layouts based on it use the hooks. The standalone search layout also uses them. A custom layout or copied head/scripts include only has the insertion points its own code preserves; the theme cannot add a missing hook to an independent layout.   The source of custom.scss includes the front matter delimiters before its rules:   --- --- body {   line-height: 1.6; }   The HTML hooks accept HTML, including provider scripts or stylesheet links; plain CSS belongs in the CSS file. Script execution still depends on the provider, browser policy and dependency order.   Integration constraints   Google Analytics and development GoatCounter have built-in settings; a duplicate custom embed can count twice. GoatCounter is absent from v2.1.0. Favicons need URLs matching the site’s deployed baseurl; see the favicon task. The giscus hook is provider-specific and separate from these site-wide insertion points.

title: Migration field mappings
subtitle: Legacy patterns, supported fields and integration constraints
excerpt: Lookup for an existing Jekyll site’s migration. The entries below are commonpatterns to review, not automatic conversions or guarantees about anothertheme’s behavior. The procedure and publication checklist are inMigrating from another Jekyll theme.
content: Lookup for an existing Jekyll site’s migration. The entries below are common patterns to review, not automatic conversions or guarantees about another theme’s behavior. The procedure and publication checklist are in Migrating from another Jekyll theme. Layouts and page front matter Explicit page values take precedence over configuration defaults. The mappings for ordinary posts and pages use the built-in default layout. Existing setting or purpose Field or combination in Chulapa Constraint or reference layout: post for an article layout: default, header_type: post Layout reference. layout: page for a regular page layout: default, header_type: base Standalone page addresses still follow their configured permalink. image or cover for a header photograph header_img with a suitable header_type The old field is not translated; header options specify the supported types. toc: true show_toc: true TOC options. Page comments: true show_comments: true Also needs the site provider and a comment-capable layout. Page search: false include_on_search: false Local Lunr/Fuse/Simple-Jekyll-Search indexes only; not an Algolia exclusion or Google crawler directive. Post or collection document in built-in feeds include_on_feed: true Requires a resolved date; set collection dates explicitly for Jekyll 3/4 consistency and output: true to publish linked collection articles. Standalone pages are not selected. Feed constraints. Standard fields such as title, date, categories, tags and intended permalink values remain relevant. Old theme-specific include names and CSS classes have no automatic mapping; supported alternatives are in the layout and snippet reference. Front matter specimen for an ordinary dated article: --- layout: default header_type: post title: A migrated article date: 2024-01-02 show_date: true include_on_feed: true --- Site configuration and integrations Purpose Fields or output Constraint or reference Site author stored as a plain string author mapping with name Other profile fields are in Site author; guest page authors have their own mapping. Appearance chulapa-skin.skin Exact supported skin name; fonts/color overrides remain separate. Theming reference. Navbar navbar.nav entries: title, url, optional child One dropdown level; old links are not imported. Navbar. Footer footer.links entries: label, icon, url; footer.copyright Old links/copyright are not translated. Footer.
