Current Cactus/Welcomments limitations and local corrections are in Comments. Existing subscriber addresses /atom.xml, /rss.xml, optional jekyll-feed /feed.xml Built-in feeds select dated posts/collection documents with include_on_feed: true; collection output must publish linked articles. jekyll-feed’s default path can coexist; two generators must not write the same path. Google Analytics 4 gtag_id Existing measurement ID; duplicate custom tracking scripts can count twice. GA reference. GoatCounter goatcounter Requires main after v2.1.0; version and production constraints. Site-author and skin specimen (independent of page front matter): author: name: "Ana" chulapa-skin: skin: journal Local overrides and release boundary Local files matching theme paths in _layouts, _includes or assets override theme files, for both remote and gem themes. Supported insertion points and custom CSS are cataloged in Custom hooks. Changing a parent layout does not translate...

title: How publishing fits together
subtitle: The relationship between your files, the theme and the live website
excerpt: A saved file and a published web page are different things. The repository holdsthe source; a build turns it into a website; a hosting service makes the resultavailable to visitors. This distinction explains why an edit can be visible onGitHub before it appears on your site.
content: A saved file and a published web page are different things. The repository holds the source; a build turns it into a website; a hosting service makes the result available to visitors. This distinction explains why an edit can be visible on GitHub before it appears on your site.   The parts and their roles   GitHub stores the files in a repository. Jekyll turns the content and settings into web pages. Chulapa supplies their design and supported features. GitHub Pages hosts the finished website.   With the starter template, GitHub Actions runs the publishing workflow when changes reach its publishing branch. Actions runs the build and deployment; it is not the theme or the place where readers visit the finished pages. Other Jekyll sites can use different build and hosting services.   Why saving does not always change the website   A commit records an edit in a branch. The public site reflects a successfully published build, which can take time and can fail. An edit on a separate branch or a pull-request preview does not by itself replace the public website.   The Markdown filename is also not necessarily the public page address. Jekyll’s permalink settings and a site’s repository path can affect that address. Preserving those settings matters when migrating an established site.   Local preview and browser editing   A local preview runs on your own computer. It can help you check a change, but it does not publish that change for visitors. The starter’s browser-based path uses GitHub’s editor and Actions instead, so a first publication does not require installing Ruby or understanding the build tooling in advance.   For a guided first result, use Publish your first site. For an existing edit that has not appeared, use Find missing changes.

title: Accessibility and resource-loading reference
subtitle: Expected behavior, version boundaries and limits
excerpt: Lookup for the theme’s behavior and limits. Practical verification steps are inCheck accessibility and performance.
content: Lookup for the theme’s behavior and limits. Practical verification steps are in Check accessibility and performance. The improvements listed here are available on main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), not in the v2.1.0 gem or pinned remote theme. Actual results depend on content, colors, integrations and local overrides. No theme setting or test score establishes WCAG compliance for a complete site. Keyboard navigation Version: the keyboard/focus improvements below and PhotoSwipe require main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev); they are not included in the v2.1.0 gem or pin. Component Expected behavior in the development version Skip link First Tab stop, bypassing repeated navigation. Floating menu Enter/Space opens; Escape closes and returns focus to its button. Following a link closes it. Closed links are outside the Tab order. Dropdowns Native buttons; font inherits the surrounding menu styling. Sidebar TOC Close control and links are keyboard reachable while open. Escape closes and returns focus; the panel is not a modal focus trap. Active TOC section Reading-position highlight does not move keyboard focus. PhotoSwipe Arrow-key browsing and Escape closing; focus returns to the image link. Image links remain usable if the viewer cannot load. Without JavaScript, the floating menu exposes ordinary navigation links. Interactive integrations can still depend on JavaScript and network access. Custom layouts/widgets only have the semantics and controls their own markup preserves. Colors, content and motion The link/focus improvements here require main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), not the v2.1.0 gem or pin. Article links are underlined and keyboard focus is visible. Custom colors can weaken those cues or their contrast. Skin selection does not replace a check of the actual text, links and backgrounds used by a site. The carousel motion/control improvements in this paragraph require main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), not the v2.1.0 gem or pin. Automatically cycling multi-image carousels have a play/pause control with an action-specific accessible name and a plain-symbol fallback when icon assets are unavailable. Reduced motion starts them paused. Slide/navigation interaction stops rotation until explicit restart; hovering pauses temporarily. interval=0 disables cycling. Carousel reference. Video name supplies a descriptive player name, not captions or transcripts. Mermaid (available on main after v2.1.0, not in the v2.1.0 gem or pin) uses accTitle and accDescr to describe a diagram; complex content still needs a prose equivalent. Gallery snippets use generic image descriptions; individual informative photographs need descriptive custom image markup. Media tasks cover adding that content. Long titles and enlarged text are covered by representative checks, not by a promise about every custom layout or widget. Resource loading Integration or resource Loading behavior or constraint PhotoSwipe Available on main after v2.1.0, not in the v2.1.0 gem or pin; viewer loads when an image is opened. Deferred YouTube Preview first, player on activation; loading reference. MathJax Page opt-in; unnecessary enabled integrations can add resources. Mermaid Page opt-in; available on main after v2.1.0, not in the v2.1.0 gem or pin. Cactus Conditional scripts/styles on show_comments: true pages require main after v2.1.0; v2.1.0 loads those resources more broadly. Analytics Optional; configuring GA and GoatCounter enables both counters. GoatCounter...

title: Add an information or warning box
subtitle: Highlight a short message in an existing article
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page. Open its file in yourrepository and edit the article body, below the settings block between ---lines. The example uses the sample site’s kramdown Markdown parser.
content: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page. Open its file in your repository and edit the article body, below the settings block between --- lines. The example uses the sample site’s kramdown Markdown parser.   Insert the message   Separate the message from the preceding paragraph or list with a blank line. Place the attribute line immediately after the message, without a blank line between them:   Useful information for readers. {: .alert .alert-info .p-3 .mx-2 .mb-3}   Replace the message with your text. Use ordinary paragraphs for routine prose; for a concrete mistake readers need to avoid or fix, replace alert-info with alert-warning. Keep the spacing classes and keep the box short. Additional styles are in Bootstrap’s alert reference.   Publish and verify   Commit to the publishing branch and wait for Actions to succeed. Open the published article and check that the message is a padded box and the following paragraph is outside it. Check a narrow screen too.   If the attribute line appears as text, check your Markdown parser/settings against the Markdown reference. If the wrong content is inside the box, restore the blank line before the message and keep its attribute line directly attached. For an old public page, use publishing checks.   Example output:   Useful information for readers.

title: Add a caption below an image
subtitle: Keep the visible caption separate from alternative text
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with an uploaded image.For uploading and checking the path, follow Add an image first.The example uses the sample site’s kramdown Markdown parser.
content: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page with an uploaded image. For uploading and checking the path, follow Add an image first. The example uses the sample site’s kramdown Markdown parser.   Add the caption paragraph   Below the settings block at the top of the article, use your image followed by a separate paragraph and its attribute line:   ![A riverside path beneath green trees]({{ '/assets/img/river.jpg' | relative_url }})  The riverside path in spring. {: .caption}   Replace the path with your uploaded file and both descriptions with text about your photograph. Keep relative_url for a repository-based site. The caption is visible to readers; it does not replace the alternative text in square brackets. Keep a blank line before the caption and no blank line between it and {: .caption}.   Publish and verify   Commit on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the article on your website. Check that the image loads and that the caption appears below it with caption styling. Check it on a narrow screen.   For a missing image, follow the image checks. If the class text is visible or attaches to the wrong paragraph, check the blank lines and your Markdown parser. For a stale public page, use publishing checks.

title: Add a footnote to an article
subtitle: Link a source note from a sentence in your text
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page using kramdown, as in thesample configuration. Edit the article body below its settings block.
content: Use this guide for an existing Markdown post or page using kramdown, as in the sample configuration. Edit the article body below its settings block.   Add a matching reference and definition   Insert a reference after the sentence and a definition elsewhere in the same article, separated from surrounding paragraphs:   This claim has a source.[^source]  [^source]: Details about the source.   Replace the sample sentence and note with your content. The label source must match in both places; use a different label for each separate note. The rendered number is generated by the Markdown parser, not by the label’s text.   Publish and verify   Commit on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published article. Follow the superscript link to the note, then its return link to the sentence. Check that both links are keyboard reachable.   If the notation remains plain text or the note is missing, check matching labels and your parser’s footnote support in the Markdown reference. For an old public page, use publishing checks.   Example output:   This claim has a source.1                  Details about the source. ↑

title: Add a favicon
subtitle: Publish an icon with a repository-safe address
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing site. The browser-tab icon is a favicon; it isseparate from the site’s logo or article images.
content: Use this guide for an existing site. The browser-tab icon is a favicon; it is separate from the site’s logo or article images.   Upload an icon   Generate an icon package at RealFaviconGenerator and download it. Upload the extracted files to assets/favicon/ in your repository, preserving any files already there. The example below assumes the package includes favicon.ico; match the filename and capitalization to your actual file.   Link the icon from the head   Create or edit _includes/custom/custom_head.html. Keep existing snippets and edit any existing favicon link instead of adding a competing copy. For the ICO file above, this is a complete icon link:   <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="{{ '/assets/favicon/favicon.ico' | relative_url }}">   Keep relative_url: it adds the site’s baseurl for project sites. Do not put /my-blog in the path yourself or paste a second <head> element into the hook.   For a fuller generated package, use its HTML instead, adjusting every icon URL to the deployed location. Configure the generator for that location, including baseurl, or use relative_url for site-relative paths. Check any manifest’s internal icon paths too. Do not assume adding an icon/manifest provides offline support or app installability.   Browsers can also discover favicon.ico at the domain root. A file at the root of a project repository is not necessarily at the domain root; use the explicit link above for a site under /repository.   Publish and verify   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published site. Inspect its HTML source and open the icon URL: a project site should include its repository path, such as /my-blog/assets/favicon/favicon.ico. Verify the file loads rather than returning a 404, then check the browser tab.   If the tab still shows an old icon while the URL loads the new file, try a fresh tab or browser session; browsers can cache favicons. For a missing file, check its upload, exact name and generated path. For missing head HTML, use the custom-head checks.

title: Use the Chulapa font
subtitle: Apply the bundled font to headings or selected text
excerpt: Use this guide on an existing site using the theme’s stylesheets. TheChulapa font is already supplied by the theme; no Google Fonts setup is needed.
content: Use this guide on an existing site using the theme’s stylesheets. The Chulapa font is already supplied by the theme; no Google Fonts setup is needed.   Apply it to headings   In _config.yml, edit your existing chulapa-skin.vars mapping, keeping your skin and other overrides. Add or update this family; do not create a second chulapa-skin section:   chulapa-skin:   vars:     headings-font-family: "chulapa, sans-serif"   To enable its distinctive ligatures, append these rules to assets/css/custom.scss, preserving existing rules and its empty YAML front matter. If the file does not exist, the complete example is:   --- --- h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6 {     -webkit-font-feature-settings: "liga", "dlig";     -moz-font-feature-settings: "liga=1, dlig=1";     -moz-font-feature-settings: "liga", "dlig";     -ms-font-feature-settings: "liga", "dlig";     -o-font-feature-settings: "liga", "dlig";     font-feature-settings: "liga", "dlig";     text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; }   For an existing file, append only the rules; do not add another pair of front matter delimiters. For other font families, use Change the fonts.   Apply it to selected text instead   If you only want the font on selected text, keep your heading configuration and use the existing chulapa class in a Markdown article. The class supplies both the font and ligature styling:   <span class="chulapa">Chulapa</span>   For a whole paragraph with kramdown, put the attribute line directly after it:   A relaxing cup of café con leche in Plaza Mayor. {: .chulapa}   Publish and verify   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open an article on the website. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml. Compare the headings or selected text with an ordinary paragraph.   If the font appears as ordinary letters without the distinctive ligatures, check the CSS rules/class and any later overrides. Without ligatures it looks like Chulapa; with the class it looks like Chulapa. Check the compiled CSS and font requests in your browser. On main after v2.1.0 (v2.1.1-dev), preload/CSS use theme-local font assets with baseurl; that loading improvement is not in the v2.1.0 release. For an older theme version, check the font URL its own stylesheet uses. For old public content, use publishing checks.

title: Add a Font Awesome icon to an article
subtitle: Place an icon in Markdown without losing its meaning
excerpt: Use this guide on an existing site using the theme’s stylesheets. Font Awesomeis already loaded; do not add another script or stylesheet to the article.
content: Use this guide on an existing site using the theme’s stylesheets. Font Awesome is already loaded; do not add another script or stylesheet to the article.   Insert the icon   Edit a post or page’s .md file. Below its front matter (the settings between --- lines), paste this complete example, keeping the surrounding text:   <i class="fas fa-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i> Check the publication date.    Check the publication date.   The text carries the meaning; aria-hidden="true" keeps the decorative icon from being announced again by screen readers. Do not replace a link or button’s accessible name with an icon alone.   To choose another icon, use the Font Awesome catalog. Copy the classes for a free icon available in your configured version; a paid icon or a class from a different version may not display. Replace only the example’s classes and text, retaining aria-hidden="true" for decorative icons.   Publish and check   Commit the article on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published page. The GitHub Markdown preview does not establish that the site’s icon stylesheet loaded. Check that the icon and its explanatory text both appear, including on a narrow screen.   If the icon is missing, check its spelling and whether it is available in your Font Awesome version or kit. Inspect failed stylesheet/kit requests in the browser’s developer tools; blocked external resources can prevent rendering. Do not add duplicate loaders as a workaround.   For version selection, v4 compatibility and kit settings, use the Font Awesome reference.

title: Check which theme version your site uses
subtitle: Identify the selected release before troubleshooting or upgrading
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing site when an option does not match itsdocumentation or you need to identify your current release. These checks do notupgrade the theme.
content: Use this guide for an existing site when an option does not match its documentation or you need to identify your current release. These checks do not upgrade the theme.   Check the selected theme   For a remote-theme installation, open _config.yml and find remote_theme:   remote_theme: dieghernan/chulapa@v2.1.0   Here, @v2.1.0 selects that release. An unpinned value such as dieghernan/chulapa follows the repository’s default branch; it does not select a fixed release. An explicit branch can move too. Record the value you actually have rather than replacing it with this example.   For a gem installation, open Gemfile.lock and find the chulapa-jekyll entry and its resolved version. The Gemfile’s version requirement alone may allow more than one version. If you have no lockfile, this check cannot identify the resolved gem used for the build; inspect the publishing build’s dependency output.   Compare with the published website   Open the published page’s HTML source and search for this comment near the beginning, replacing the example text with the version displayed:   <!-- Chulapa Jekyll Theme - VERSION NUMBER HERE -->   This marker is present on pages using the theme’s head include. If it is absent, check whether a local layout or head include replaced it. If the page is old, verify the publishing run and website address.   The marker is not an exact commit identifier. It cannot identify a specific unpinned remote-theme revision or describe local overrides. A version selected in source also does not prove that the latest build has been published.   Keep the configured tag or resolved gem version with your troubleshooting notes. Before relying on a documented feature, check its release caveat. When ready to change versions, use the remote-theme or gem installation guide, and review local overrides.

title: Publish posts in the built-in feeds
subtitle: Include articles and share a subscription address
excerpt: Use this guide on an existing site to let readers subscribe in a feed reader.The theme supplies Atom at /atom.xml and RSS 2.0 at /rss.xml; you do not needto install jekyll-feed for these addresses.
content: Use this guide on an existing site to let readers subscribe in a feed reader. The theme supplies Atom at /atom.xml and RSS 2.0 at /rss.xml; you do not need to install jekyll-feed for these addresses.   Include your posts   In _config.yml, find the existing defaults list. For an existing scope with path: "" and type: posts, add include_on_feed: true under its values, preserving the other values. If that scope is missing, append the following list item under defaults. Create the complete section only if it is absent:   defaults:   - scope:       path: ""       type: posts     values:       include_on_feed: true   Use the YAML boolean true, without quotes. An explicit value in a post’s front matter takes precedence over the default. To keep a particular post out, set include_on_feed: false in its existing front matter.   The built-in feeds select posts and collection documents with include_on_feed: true and a date. Posts get their date from the filename; for a collection document, first ensure its existing entry under collections in _config.yml has output: true so its article URL is published. Preserve the other collection settings. Then set date explicitly in its front matter to control its publication date and ordering. Jekyll 4 can infer a date when none is set; do not rely on that behavior across Jekyll versions. An ordinary standalone page outside a collection is not selected just by adding these settings. See the field reference.   Publish and share the address   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open /atom.xml on your published site, including its repository path if it has one: for example, https://example.github.io/my-blog/atom.xml. Check /rss.xml too. Open the feed in a feed reader and confirm that a recent, published post appears and its link opens the expected article. A browser may display XML or download the file; that alone is not a failure.   Follow Edit footer links to add a labelled subscription link using url: /atom.xml or url: /rss.xml. Keep other footer links and omit the repository prefix in this setting; the theme adds baseurl.   If a post is missing, check its explicit include_on_feed value and date, any more-specific defaults, and whether the publishing build included it. Use Find missing changes before changing feed addresses. If a collection entry appears but its article returns 404, check that the collection has output: true, rebuild, and open that article URL directly. Opting a document into the feed does not enable collection output. If a feed returns 404, check the URL, latest deployment and any local file that overrides the theme’s feed asset.   Already have subscribers at /feed.xml? Keep that address working; use Keep a jekyll-feed subscription address instead of silently switching readers to another URL.

title: Keep a jekyll-feed subscription address
subtitle: Preserve an existing feed alongside the theme's Atom and RSS files
excerpt: Use this guide when your existing site uses jekyll-feed, especially if readersalready subscribe to /feed.xml. If you only need a new subscription feed, usethe built-in feeds without another plugin.
content: Use this guide when your existing site uses jekyll-feed, especially if readers already subscribe to /feed.xml. If you only need a new subscription feed, use the built-in feeds without another plugin.   Check the plugin and its address   Keep your existing jekyll-feed dependency and plugin entry. If it is not yet installed but you need it, follow its installation guide for your publishing setup. Preserve the other Gemfile dependencies and _config.yml plugins; the theme’s include_on_feed setting does not configure the plugin’s selection of posts.   Check the existing feed.path setting in _config.yml. The plugin’s default /feed.xml can coexist with the theme’s /atom.xml and /rss.xml. Keep the existing subscription address unless you have a separate plan for subscribers.   Avoid duplicate output paths. Pointing jekyll-feed at /atom.xml or /rss.xml while the theme generates the same file creates a collision. Do not use that path as a quick replacement or assume the last generated file is stable.   If your existing plugin already uses one of those addresses, resolve the collision before publishing. This guide covers coexistence at separate URLs; it does not provide a switch to disable the theme’s feeds. Review existing local overrides and the plugin’s configuration rather than inventing a YAML flag or simply deleting a URL readers use.   Publish and verify   Commit to the publishing branch and wait for Actions to succeed. Open the existing subscription URL on the published site, including baseurl for a project site. Add it to a feed reader, check a recent entry and follow its link. Check /atom.xml and /rss.xml as well if you retain the built-in feeds.   Follow Edit footer links to keep the subscription link at its chosen address, such as url: /feed.xml, without a repository prefix. The theme’s standard head still advertises its built-in Atom and RSS feeds; adding the plugin or changing a footer link does not replace those head links.   If the plugin feed is missing, check that the publishing environment loads jekyll-feed, its configured path and any same-path files. If the entries are unexpected, use the plugin’s own configuration documentation; do not try to control it with the theme’s include_on_feed field.

title: Add a table of contents inside an article
subtitle: Insert heading links into the Markdown content
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing post or page rendered with kramdown. It adds anindex of heading links where you place it in the article’s text.
content: Use this guide for an existing post or page rendered with kramdown. It adds an index of heading links where you place it in the article’s text.   The two TOCs have different settings. This task uses Markdown’s {:toc} marker; the layout’s automatic TOC uses show_toc, h_min and h_max. Both exclude headings marked .no_toc. See the layout options.   Insert the marker   Edit the article’s .md file. Keep its existing front matter (the settings between --- lines). In the content below it, at the position where you want the index to appear, add these two lines with a blank line above and below:   * Contents {:toc}   Keep the marker and attribute on separate lines. Contents is a placeholder replaced by generated links; use 1. Contents instead of * Contents for a numbered list. The index covers eligible headings throughout the article, including headings before the marker. Moving the marker does not limit its scope; use heading exclusions or toc_levels to control the entries.   Keep real Markdown headings in the article, such as ## First section and ### Details. To omit a particular heading from this content index, place the attribute immediately below that heading:   ## Further reading {:.no_toc}   The .no_toc class also excludes this heading from the theme’s automatic TOC when show_toc or show_sidetoc is enabled. It is not an exclusion for only one of the two indexes.   Limit the heading levels when needed   To list only levels 2 through 6, edit the existing kramdown mapping in _config.yml, preserving its parser and other settings. Add or update toc_levels; create the mapping only if it is missing:   kramdown:   toc_levels: 2..6   This setting affects kramdown content indexes across the site, not just this article. It does not change the theme’s automatic TOC. Skip this edit if your current heading range already suits your articles.   Publish and check   Commit the article and any configuration edit on the publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the published article. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after changing _config.yml.   Check that the placeholder became links, that selecting a link reaches its heading, and that an excluded heading is absent. Check on a narrow screen too. If the marker remains plain text, check the two-line syntax, blank lines and whether it was placed inside a code fence. The GitHub file preview does not establish the published result.   The sample site uses kramdown with the GFM parser. Other parser combinations can differ; verify generated output before changing the site-wide parser. Use the Markdown syntax reference for specimens and publishing checks for old output.

title: Publish an illustrated page and add it to the menu
subtitle: A second browser-only tutorial for your published blog
excerpt: Create a photo page with the starter's image, add its menu link and check the published result.
content: In this tutorial, you will publish a page called My photo walk, with a photograph of Madrid and a Photo walk menu link. Follow the supplied names and text so you can check each result; personalize them after finishing. Start with the blog you published in Publish your first site. You need its repository open on GitHub and the existing assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg photograph from the Chulapa 101 template. No local software is needed. If that file is missing, restore the starter photograph before starting. 1. Create the photo page In your repository’s Code tab, choose Add file > Create new file. Name the file _pages/photo-walk.md and paste this complete example: --- layout: default header_type: base title: "My photo walk" permalink: /photo-walk/ --- ## An evening in Madrid ![Buildings illuminated at night in Madrid]({{ '/assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg' | relative_url }}) This is my first illustrated page. Keep both --- lines and the image expression exactly as shown. The expression makes the photograph’s address work when the site is under a repository path. The words in square brackets describe the photograph for readers who cannot see it. Click Commit changes and save on the same default branch used in the first tutorial. Do not overwrite an existing file or page at /photo-walk/; this exercise assumes that address is unused. Check: _pages/photo-walk.md appears in your repository with the title, heading, photograph expression and sentence above. 2. Add the menu link Open _config.yml in Code and click the pencil button. Find the existing navbar section, its nav list, and the Categories entry. Immediately after its url: /categories/ line, add these two lines: - title: Photo walk url: /photo-walk/ Align the new dash with the existing menu-entry dashes and align url with title. Keep About, Archive, Tags, Categories and the other site settings. Do not add another navbar section or prefix /photo-walk/ with your repository name. Click Commit changes on the same branch. Check: the existing menu entries remain, followed by Photo walk with url: /photo-walk/. The menu label and page title can differ; here we use Photo walk for the menu and My photo walk for the page. 3. Open your published page In Actions, wait for the publishing run for your latest saved change to finish successfully. Open the website address from Settings > Pages. Follow Photo walk in the menu. On a narrow screen, open the menu first. Check: the page shows My photo walk, An evening in Madrid, the Madrid photograph and This is my first illustrated page. Open Home, then follow Photo walk again to confirm that visitors can reach it from the site. You have published a new illustrated page and made it reachable from the menu. You can now replace its text and photograph while keeping its public address. If the result is missing, use the publishing checks and return to the checks above. If the image is missing, compare its exact filename and expression with step 1. Creating the file and adding a menu link are separate edits; check that...

title: Identify a personal site's publisher
subtitle: Set Person in search metadata without changing article authors
excerpt: Configure the publisher of a personal blog and verify the generated structured data.
content: Use this guide for a personal blog that you publish yourself. It changes the publisher recorded in structured data, the machine-readable description supplied to search engines. It does not change the author shown on an article or the site’s visible title. The publisher settings are available in v2.1.0 and later.   Edit the publisher   Open _config.yml in your repository and edit its existing publisher mapping. If none exists, add this section once, replacing the example name with yours:   publisher:   type: Person   name: Jane Doe   Keep Person with that exact capitalization and preserve unrelated settings. If your existing publisher has a logo, that field is ignored for a person; you do not need to upload an organization logo for this task.   For a person’s photograph, the theme can use the site author’s avatar. If you need a different existing image, set publisher.image in the same mapping to its uploaded path or full URL. Keep publisher.url only if you want a publisher website different from the site’s home page. Use the field reference for defaults, image fallbacks and organization settings.   Publish and inspect the result   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published home page and a post. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after editing _config.yml.   View the page’s HTML source and find the application/ld+json script describing the website or article. Inside its publisher object, check that @type is Person and name matches your publisher name. Check its url and any image URL too, including the repository path when your site uses baseurl.   The article’s author should still be its original author. A publisher identifies who publishes the site; changing it does not rewrite guest-author settings. Structured data does not guarantee a particular search result or preview.   If the publisher still says Organization, check the capitalization, duplicate publisher sections and the latest published commit. Check your theme version and local head/layout overrides if expected metadata is missing; an older local copy can override the installed theme. Use publishing checks for old output and YAML checks for a failed build.

title: Display an article date in another language
subtitle: Translate month and weekday names in your content
excerpt: Add a localized date to an existing dated article using the supplied snippet.
content: Use this guide when you want to display a date inside an existing article or custom template. You need a post with a date, or a page whose front matter explicitly sets date. The supplied snippet translates English month and weekday names into Spanish, French, German or Italian. English is the fallback.   This task changes the date text you insert. It does not change the stored date, translate the article or replace every date elsewhere on the website.   Insert the date   Open the article’s .md file. Below its front matter (the settings between the --- lines), insert this complete example, outside any code fence:   {% assign formatted_date = page.date | date: "%A %d, %B %Y" %} {% include snippets/datetranslate.html date=formatted_date lang="es-ES" %}   The first line formats the date; the second translates the month and weekday names. For an article dated 2020-02-14, this example displays viernes 14, febrero 2020. The format controls order and punctuation; the translation does not rearrange them or capitalize the names.   For another supported language, replace es-ES with fr, de or it. An unsupported language retains lowercase English names; it does not fetch a translation service.   Use the site language when appropriate   To follow the site’s existing language setting, omit the lang parameter:   {% assign formatted_date = page.date | date: "%A %d, %B %Y" %} {% include snippets/datetranslate.html date=formatted_date %}   The snippet uses locale from _config.yml, falling back to English if absent. It does not automatically use a page-level locale. Keep the explicit lang parameter for an article that needs a different date language.   Changing site locale also changes language metadata; it is not a switch that translates the whole interface. Keep it accurate for your website. Snippet parameters and supported-language behavior are in the date reference.   Publish and check   Commit to the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published article. Check the date against the article’s actual date, including month/weekday names, order and punctuation. For a local preview, restart Jekyll after editing _config.yml.   If no date appears, check that the article has a date and that both lines were saved outside the front matter. If the code appears literally, remove any code fence surrounding it in the article. GitHub’s file preview does not run the snippet. Use publishing checks if the site shows old content. For a custom template, supply its intended dated object’s value instead of assuming that every page has page.date.

title: Point a republished article to its original URL
subtitle: Set a canonical URL without changing the copied page's address
excerpt: Identify an article's original version, exclude the duplicate from a jekyll-sitemap index and verify generated metadata.
content: Use this guide when you publish a copy of an article and want its metadata to identify the original version. You need the original article’s complete public URL and an existing post or page to edit. Ordinary unique articles do not need a custom canonical URL.   Identify the original article   Open the copied article’s .md file. Inside its existing front matter (between the --- lines), add or update canonical_url, replacing the example with the actual original article address:   canonical_url: https://example.com/original-article/   Preserve the copied page’s title, intended permalink and other settings. Use the complete https:// address for an original article on another website. For an original on your own site, a path beginning with / is also accepted; it resolves using your site’s url and baseurl.   This is not a redirect. Visitors still open the copy at its existing address. The canonical URL identifies the original in generated metadata and feed links; it does not move or delete the copied page.   Exclude the copy from a generated sitemap when applicable   If your publishing setup uses jekyll-sitemap, add this to the copied article’s existing front matter:   sitemap: false   Keep false unquoted. The plugin otherwise lists the copied page’s actual URL; canonical_url does not rewrite that entry to the original address. Keep the original article in its own site’s sitemap. If you maintain a sitemap another way, review that setup separately; this field is a jekyll-sitemap control.   Do not use the same canonical override on every page of a paginated series. Those pages are distinct destinations and should retain their own canonical URLs.   Publish and verify   Commit on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the copy at its existing website address. Confirm that it still displays its content. View its HTML source and check that <link rel="canonical"> and og:url identify the original. Check the page/article JSON-LD URL too. If the article is in a built-in feed, inspect its entry’s article link: it should also identify the original.   When using jekyll-sitemap, open the published sitemap.xml and confirm that the copy’s address is absent. Check the original address directly to make sure it loads. Local builds cannot establish that an external original is reachable.   If metadata still uses the copy’s address, check spelling, the saved publishing commit and local head/layout overrides. Blank values, unsupported URL schemes and protocol-relative addresses such as //example.com/article/ fall back to the page’s own URL. Fragments are removed. See the canonical field reference and publishing checks.

title: Add tag and category indexes for your posts
subtitle: Connect article badges to grouped lists
excerpt: Use this guide on an existing blog with tagged or categorized posts. The resultis a Tags page and a Categories page whose grouped lists link to your articles.See the tag demo and category demo for renderedexamples; their collection choices differ from this post-only setup.
content: Use this guide on an existing blog with tagged or categorized posts. The result is a Tags page and a Categories page whose grouped lists link to your articles. See the tag demo and category demo for rendered examples; their collection choices differ from this post-only setup.   Create or update the index pages   In the starter, edit _pages/tags.md and _pages/categories.md. If a page already exists, update its existing settings and keep unrelated front matter/content; do not create a second file at the same public address. For a new page, use these complete examples.   Tags page, _pages/tags.md:   --- layout: cloudtag title: Tags permalink: /tags/ include_collection: posts ---  Browse posts by tag.   Categories page, _pages/categories.md:   --- layout: cloudcategory title: Categories permalink: /categories/ include_collection: posts ---  Browse posts by category.   Without the starter’s _pages setup, create tags.md and categories.md beside _config.yml instead. Preserve existing public paths when adapting an established site, and use those same paths in the next step.   Connect the article badges   In _config.yml, edit the existing defaults entry whose scope has path: "" and type: posts. Merge these fields into its values, keeping its layout, header and other settings. Add this complete mapping only if none exists:   defaults:   - scope:       path: ""       type: posts     values:       cloudtag_url: /tags/       cloudcategory_url: /categories/       show_tags: true       show_categories: true   Do not add a second defaults key. Explicit values on a post override defaults. Use paths without the repository prefix: the theme adds baseurl.   Edit an existing post with the default layout, preserving its other settings, and add tags/categories inside its front matter. For example:   tags:   - city walks categories:   - travel   For another existing collection, use its name without _ in both the defaults scope and include_collection. Its linked articles need output: true under the existing collection configuration to be published. Ordinary standalone pages are not part of these collection indexes. Full scope/alias details remain in the layout reference.   Publish and verify   Commit the page, configuration and post edits on the publishing branch. Wait for Actions to succeed, then open the article. Follow its tag/category badges and check that they reach the matching group, that the article is listed and that its link opens the article. Check the group buttons on the index and a narrow screen too. Add menu links with Edit a menu link if wanted.   For missing badges, check show_tags/show_categories, actual post labels and explicit front matter overrides. For a 404 or missing group, compare the public permalink, badge URL, exact labels and collection scope. Both the page and badge settings are needed; a menu link does not create the page. Use publishing checks for old output.   In the development version after v2.1.0, group fragments preserve tag/category names and replace spaces with hyphens: demo links to #demo, and demo topic to #demo-topic. This also fixes badge links for names containing demo, which older versions rewrote only in the cloud index. Update any manually written links to those older dmo fragments when upgrading.

title: Set a post's sharing text and images
subtitle: Prepare metadata without changing the visible article
excerpt: Use this guide for an existing post when you want a specific description andimage in its sharing metadata. The theme supplies the tags; do not paste anotherOpen Graph or JSON-LD block into a custom head hook.
content: Use this guide for an existing post when you want a specific description and image in its sharing metadata. The theme supplies the tags; do not paste another Open Graph or JSON-LD block into a custom head hook.   Upload the image and edit the post   Upload your photograph to assets/img/article.jpg, or use the actual path of an image already in your repository. Keep its exact filename and capitalization. In the post’s existing front matter, add or update these fields, preserving the post title, date, permalink and other settings:   description: A short account of an evening walk through Madrid. og_title: An evening walk in Madrid og_image: /assets/img/article.jpg og_image_alt: A street in Madrid at night schema_image: /assets/img/article.jpg   Replace the text and image path with your own. description supplies metadata text and og_title supplies the sharing title; they do not replace the article’s visible heading. og_image supplies its social image and schema_image supplies the illustration URLs in a post’s BlogPosting structured data. A regular page’s structured data does not become an article merely by setting schema_image.   These fields do not insert a photograph into the article body. Use Add an image for visible content. Keep header_img only if you also want a header image. If you have several existing article illustrations, the image reference accepts a list; the theme does not generate crops or inspect dimensions. Supply width/height/type only when known and accurate, using the social image fields.   Publish and inspect the metadata   Commit the image and post edits, wait for Actions to succeed and open the published post. Inspect its HTML source: check og:title, the description, og:image and its alt text. In the BlogPosting JSON-LD script, check the image array. Open each generated image URL and confirm it loads, including the repository path on project sites. Check the visible article heading is unchanged.   The Welcome post is a live example with an explicit article image and a header photograph. Its source shows the actual values; the field reference keeps the complete fallback rules.   If sharing still shows old data, first check the published source and image URL, then refresh the preview using the sharing service’s tools when available. Services can cache previews and choose different crops or text. Correct metadata does not guarantee a particular preview or search result. Use publishing checks if the source itself is old.

title: Keep an auxiliary page out of search results
subtitle: Configure external indexing, sitemap entries and local search separately
excerpt: Use this guide for a published auxiliary page, such as a search-results page,that should remain directly accessible without appearing in indexes. Thesesettings are independent; choose the ones that match your publishing setup.
content: Use this guide for a published auxiliary page, such as a search-results page, that should remain directly accessible without appearing in indexes. These settings are independent; choose the ones that match your publishing setup.   Excluding a page is not access control. Its public URL still works. These settings do not make private information safe to publish.   Edit the existing page   Inside the page’s current front matter, add or update these fields while keeping its title, layout and permalink:   robots: "noindex, follow" sitemap: false include_on_search: false   robots asks external crawlers not to index the page. Crawlers need to access it to read the instruction; do not block it in robots.txt and assume they can still read noindex. Removal from existing search results is not immediate.   sitemap: false excludes it from jekyll-sitemap if that plugin generates your sitemap. It does not itself prevent external indexing. include_on_search: false excludes it from the built-in Lunr, Fuse.js and Simple-Jekyll-Search indexes.   For Algolia, configure its files_to_exclude for the source file and upload the updated index using the Algolia guide. The local-search flag is not an Algolia exclusion. Google Custom Search uses external indexing rather than these local index files. Other sitemap/index tools need their own configuration.   Publish and verify   Commit on the publishing branch, wait for Actions to succeed and open the page directly. Check its content still loads and its HTML source contains the noindex, follow robots value. With jekyll-sitemap, check the page’s actual URL is absent from the published sitemap.xml.   For local search, search for a distinctive phrase from the page after rebuilding and check that the page no longer appears. For Algolia, verify the updated uploaded records separately. The documentation’s Search page uses these three fields; its source is a real configuration example, not evidence of immediate removal by a crawler.   If the result is unexpected, check explicit front matter and more-specific configuration defaults, the actual search provider and the latest publishing run. Use the field constraints and publishing checks. Do not assume tags, archives, error pages or pagination are automatically excluded by their layout or path.

title: Syntax highlighting reference
subtitle: Available styles and rendered code specimens
excerpt: Browse available syntax highlighting styles and compare rendered code examples.
content: Lookup for highlighting style identifiers and code specimens. The selector previews a style on this page and displays its configuration mapping. For the editing and publishing procedure, use Change code highlighting. Changing this preview does not save the style on your own website. Select style None chulapa-skin: highlight: Code specimens The examples below show the selected stylesheet across code languages. JavaScript // Cross-browser xml parsing var parseXML = function( data ) { var xml, tmp; if ( !data || typeof data !== "string" ) { return null; } try { if ( window.DOMParser ) { // Standard tmp = new DOMParser(); xml = tmp.parseFromString( data , "text/xml" ); } else { // IE xml = new ActiveXObject( "Microsoft.XMLDOM" ); xml.async = false; xml.loadXML( data ); } } catch( e ) { xml = undefined; } if ( !xml || !xml.documentElement || xml.getElementsByTagName( "parsererror" ).length ) { jQuery.error( "Invalid XML: " + data ); } return xml; }; // Bind a function to a context, optionally partially applying any arguments. var proxy = function( fn, context ) { var tmp, args, proxy; if ( typeof context === "string" ) { tmp = fn[ context ]; context = fn; fn = tmp; } // Quick check to determine if target is callable, in the spec // this throws a TypeError, but we will just return undefined. if ( !jQuery.isFunction( fn ) ) { return undefined; content: Developed by dieghernan. To use this skin, update the following settings in _config.yml: chulapa-skin: skin : navi autothemer : # Set to true to derive undefined colors vars : ... Autothemer fills in colors that the skin and vars have not defined. It does not override existing values, so its visible effect depends on the skin. Use vars to override specific colors. See the autothemer guide.
